newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher profit surge prompts upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher profit surge prompts upgrades.

text.p: Profit forecasts for Kingfisher Plc were upgraded on Wednesday after the retailer reported a 47 percent jump in half year profits to 109.6 million stg.
Analysts said they understood UBS had increased its pre-tax profit forecast for 1996/97 to 355 million stg from 340 million and retained its positive stance on the stock.
One analyst, who asked to remain anonymous, said he was increasing to 370 million stg from 350 million and the top of the market range was now 380 million stg.
Last year Kingfisher made profits of 311.7 million stg.
Another analyst said, "There's still plenty more in the pipeline at B&Q and better news to come."
B&Q, Kingfisher's home improvement chain, boosted profits by nearly 48 percent to 47.0 million stg.

Some analysts advised a more cautious "hold" on the shares, which had risen sharply ahead of the results. They also expressed concern about prospects for Darty, the French electricals retailer, because of the depressed state of French market. Darty accounts for about 30 percent of group profits.
Kingfisher's shares were 10 pence higher at 675 pence by 1347 GMT. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
